feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. Iteration 4 (16 mm footprints, y=0.05 m, wheel_track 0.08 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, mass 0.8 kg, score 58.54) is still the best. Iteration 8 showed that moving the sensors to y=0.03 m cost about 17 points (41.1), so the lead should stay at y=0.05 m. Iterations 5, 6 and 7 showed that wheel_radius 0.04 m (41.4), mass 1.0 kg (42.7) and wheel_radius 0.025 m (57.9) all score below the 0.03 m, 0.8 kg layout, so those values stay. Iteration 1 to 4 showed that line loss falls as the sensor span widens, and the span at +/-0.06 m with 12 mm footprints is now the open question. I kept the iteration 4 controller so the footprint change is isolated. When the next race reports: if the s-bend and slalom max_error or steering_oscillation falls, the sharper readings are helping, so keep 12 mm and test the span next. If line_loss_events rise above iteration 4 levels (about 0.95 on the s-bend and 0.85 on the slalom) at the outer sensors, return to 16 mm before changing anything else.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events rise above iteration 4 levels on the s-bend or slalom while max_error and steering_oscillation hold: keep sensor_size 0.012 m, widen the outer sensors from x=+/-0.06 m to x=+/-0.07 m (seven sensors, spacing about 0.0233 m). Evidence: iterations 1 to 4 showed that widening the span cut line loss from about 1.0 to about 0.85 per run, so a wider span is the way to recover edge coverage.

If line loss rises and the 12 mm footprint is not clearly lowering max_error: return sensor_size to 0.016 m and keep the iteration 4 layout (y=0.05 m, +/-0.06 m span). Evidence: iteration 4 is the best design at 58.54, and iteration 8 showed that moving the sensors away from it cost about 17 points.

Keep wheel_track 0.08 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, mass 0.8 kg, body 0.18 x 0.12 m and y=0.05 m unchanged. Evidence: iterations 5 to 8 each moved one of these and scored 41.4, 42.7, 57.9 and 41.1, all below iteration 4 (58.54).
